question: GQ-007
subject: the 78 books are searchable — and three wrong diagnoses on the way

the_objection_that_did_not_apply.i_had_written: the 78 books stay unindexed because indexing needs the synthetic-gid decision I refused
the_objection_that_did_not_apply.what_i_checked: CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE passage_search USING fts5(gid UNINDEXED, ...)
the_objection_that_did_not_apply.so: UNINDEXED means FTS5 stores the column as an opaque passthrough — never compared, joined or ordered on. A TEXT id works exactly as well.
the_objection_that_did_not_apply.conclusion: "cannot join on gid" was never the same as "cannot be searched". I generalised a real constraint past its scope.

built: scripts/build-external-passages.mjs — separate index, live schema mirrored with ext_id TEXT where gid INTEGER sits

search_verified.positive: "metaphysical AND poets" returns real snippets from Images of Eternity, joined to catalogue titles
search_verified.adversarial: "zxqwvblorptik" returns 0 — the index discriminates rather than matching everything

three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.theory: multi-column OCR shreds paragraphs; hyphen-rejoin will fix it
three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.evidence: a Python test on b21471824 showed 3,679 -> 283,492 words, 77x
three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.outcome: applied to the script, corpus moved 1.66M -> 1.85M. The book itself barely improved.
three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.error: I inferred a corpus-wide cause from ONE file and reported the isolated number as if it were the fix

three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.theory: my Python mirror and the JS segmenter are different algorithms
three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.outcome: aligned them; output IDENTICAL, 26,542 passages both ways
three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.error: second guess, also wrong — and the patch landing (bytes changed) proved nothing about the diagnosis

three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.theory: measure which filter actually cuts, instead of guessing
three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.finding: the alpha-ratio filter rejected 3,208 of 3,334 long blocks
three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.cause: this OCR puts DOUBLE SPACES between every word, dragging letters/total to 0.65-0.68 against a 0.7 threshold. Whitespace is not evidence of scan noise.
three_wrong_diagnoses_in_order.fix: compute the ratio over non-space characters

the_lesson: Two guesses cost two rebuilds. The third attempt measured which filter was cutting and found it in one step. A patch that lands is not a diagnosis that holds — applyEdit proved my edits applied while the theory behind them was wrong twice.
first_real_use_of_lib_patch: all three edits went through applyEdit with post-conditions, the helper I built two turns ago and had never used
